feature: Charcoal, chalk and crayon on a paper grain, and Smudge
summary: The Brush's charcoal, chalk and crayon now catch on a paper grain, each in its own way, and a Smudge mode drags paint that is already there. Medium and Mode sit over the tool bar while the brush is in hand.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default. Open any screenshot. Walk: Scripts/playtest/brush-dry-media-and-smudge-walk.json.

try.do: Press B. Medium and Mode appear over the tool bar.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Drag across the picture: a charcoal stroke, soft, grey and dusty, streaked along the drag.
Pick Chalk from Medium and drag again; then Crayon and drag again.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Pick Charcoal, click Smudge, and drag from inside the charcoal stroke out into bare paper.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press Command Z: the smudge comes off as one step, the stroke stays.
Compare the stroke sheet (one row per medium, then the plain round tip): 2026-10-24-dry-media-sheet.png.

evaluate: Shown the three strokes without their names, could you tell charcoal from chalk?
Does the smudge feel like a finger dragging charcoal, or like a grey blur laid on top?
Is crayon's squared, striated end closer to a real crayon than the round ends the other two have?
Do Medium and Mode over the tool bar read as the brush's own options, where you would look for them?
rough: Charcoal and chalk are still too close: three blind model judges named all four rows correctly but said charcoal and chalk would not survive a blind swap, and that the three share one grain at different strengths. The task stays open on that item (charcoal-chalk-and-crayon-catch-on-a-paper-grain).
No taper, no pressure: every stroke is one width end to end, which every judge called out. That is the pressure, tilt and speed slice (pen-pressure-tilt-and-pointer-speed-shape-a-brus).

The smudge only spreads paint into lighter places; it never lifts charcoal off where the finger starts, and it carries no grain. Chose that so the live smudge shows exactly what lands; written in docs/design/brushes.md (charcoal-chalk-and-crayon-catch-on-a-paper-grain).
Smudging over a bare screenshot does nothing, by the non-destructive rule: a smudge only moves paint on a Paint layer.

The retouch walkthrough draws the brush's settings as panel rows (Size, Hardness, Flow, a mode dropdown); this slice puts only Medium and Mode over the tool bar, and the panel section with the rest is each-brush-shows-its-own-settings-in-the-tool-op.

The Medium dropdown is chosen in-process by the walk, not opened by a pointer click on its face; that proof belongs to each-brush-shows-its-own-settings-in-the-tool-op. The Mode segment is clicked at its face.

Marker, airbrush, oil and watercolour are in the Medium list and still paint with the plain round tip until their slices (marker-strokes-are-flat-and-darken-where-they-cr, watercolour-strokes-are-transparent-pool-darker, oil-paint-strokes-carry-and-smear-colour-and-sho).
Speed: a dry stroke rasterizes in about 3 ms on a 2549 by 1800 layer, off the main thread (measured in the probe). The live smudge rasterizes the paint layer once at pointer down, on the main thread.
